questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the word closest in meaning to "ubiquitous".
questions.explanation: Ubiquitous means present or found everywhere, such as mobile phones in a city.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Neither the teacher nor the students ___ ready for the program.
questions.explanation: With "neither ... nor", the verb agrees with the subject nearer to it. "Students" is plural, so the verb is "were".

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which figure of speech is used in "The classroom was a zoo after recess"?
questions.explanation: A metaphor compares two unlike things directly, without "like" or "as". The noisy classroom is called a zoo.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which sentence uses the pronoun correctly?
questions.correct: Between you and me, the test was easy.
wrong: Between you and I, the test was easy.
Between I and you, the test was easy.
Between yourself and I, the test was easy.
questions.explanation: "Between" is a preposition, so it takes the object form of the pronoun: "me", not "I".

questions.subject: Filipino
questions.question: Alin ang kasingkahulugan ng salitang "masipag"?
questions.explanation: Ang masipag ay taong laging gumagawa at nagsisikap. Ang "masikap" ang may pinakamalapit na kahulugan.

questions.subject: Filipino
questions.question: Ano ang tawag sa salitang naglalarawan sa pangngalan o panghalip?
questions.explanation: Ang pang-uri ay naglalarawan sa pangngalan o panghalip, gaya ng "matangkad" sa "matangkad na bata". Ang pang-abay ay naglalarawan sa pandiwa, pang-uri o kapwa pang-abay.

questions.subject: Filipino
questions.question: Sino ang sumulat ng nobelang "Noli Me Tangere"?
questions.explanation: Isinulat ni José Rizal ang "Noli Me Tangere" at inilathala ito noong 1887 sa Berlin. Si Francisco Balagtas ang sumulat ng "Florante at Laura".

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: A bag costs ₱1,250. It is sold at a 20% discount. What is the sale price?
questions.explanation: The discount is 20% of ₱1,250 = ₱250. The sale price is ₱1,250 − ₱250 = ₱1,000.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the next number in the sequence 2, 6, 18, 54, ...?
questions.explanation: Each number is 3 times the one before it. 54 × 3 = 162.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The average of five numbers is 18. When one number is removed, the average of the remaining four is 16. What number was removed?
questions.explanation: The five numbers add up to 5 × 18 = 90. The remaining four add up to 4 × 16 = 64. The removed number is 90 − 64 = 26.

questions.subject: Science and Technology
questions.question: Which part of a plant or animal cell holds most of its genetic material?
questions.explanation: The nucleus contains the chromosomes, which carry most of the cell's DNA. Ribosomes make proteins, and the cell membrane controls what enters and leaves the cell.

questions.subject: Science and Technology
questions.question: Which gas do green plants take in from the air to make food through photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: In photosynthesis, plants use light energy to turn carbon dioxide and water into glucose, and they release oxygen.

questions.subject: Science and Technology
questions.question: A swimmer pushes the water backward and moves forward. Which law best explains this?
questions.explanation: Newton's third law: for every action there is an equal and opposite reaction. The water pushes the swimmer forward as the swimmer pushes it back.

questions.subject: Philippine History
questions.question: Who is known as the "Brains of the Katipunan"?
questions.explanation: Emilio Jacinto wrote the Kartilya ng Katipunan and is called the Brains of the Katipunan. Apolinario Mabini is called the Brains of the Revolution.

questions.subject: Philippine History
questions.question: The Cry of Pugad Lawin in 1896, which began the Philippine Revolution against Spain, was led by:
questions.explanation: In August 1896, Andres Bonifacio and members of the Katipunan tore their cedulas at Pugad Lawin as a sign of revolt against Spain. Historians debate the exact site and date (Pugad Lawin or Balintawak; August 23 or 26); the government officially marks it as August 23, 1896, at Pugad Lawin.

questions.subject: Life and Works of Rizal
questions.question: Which novel by José Rizal is dedicated to the three priests Gomez, Burgos and Zamora (GOMBURZA)?
questions.explanation: Rizal dedicated El Filibusterismo (1891) to the memory of GOMBURZA, the priests executed in 1872. Noli Me Tangere is dedicated to the Philippines, and Florante at Laura is by Francisco Balagtas.

questions.subject: Child and Adolescent Learners
questions.question: A child understands that a ball of clay keeps the same amount when flattened, and can reason logically about concrete objects. According to Piaget, the child is in which stage?
questions.explanation: Conservation and logical thinking about concrete objects mark Piaget's concrete operational stage, usually about ages 7 to 11.

questions.subject: Child and Adolescent Learners
questions.question: According to Erik Erikson, the main psychosocial crisis of adolescence is:
questions.explanation: In adolescence, young people work out who they are and where they are going: identity vs. role confusion. Industry vs. inferiority comes earlier, in the school years.

questions.subject: Child and Adolescent Learners
questions.question: The gap between what a learner can do alone and what the learner can do with guidance is called the:
questions.explanation: Vygotsky called this gap the zone of proximal development. Scaffolding is the support a teacher gives to help the learner across it.

questions.subject: Child and Adolescent Learners
questions.question: A teacher gives a star each time pupils hand in homework on time, and on-time homework becomes more frequent. Which learning theory is the teacher applying?
questions.explanation: In operant conditioning (Skinner), a behavior followed by a reward is more likely to be repeated. The star is a positive reinforcer.

questions.subject: Curriculum and Teaching Methods
questions.question: Which is the highest level of the cognitive domain in the revised Bloom's taxonomy?
questions.explanation: The revised taxonomy (Anderson and Krathwohl, 2001), from lowest to highest: remembering, understanding, applying, analyzing, evaluating, creating.

questions.subject: Curriculum and Teaching Methods
questions.question: Which method starts with specific examples and leads learners to form the general rule themselves?
questions.explanation: The inductive method moves from specific examples to a generalization. The deductive method states the rule first, then applies it to examples.

questions.subject: Assessment of Learning
questions.question: A test that gives consistent results when taken again under the same conditions is:
questions.explanation: Reliability is consistency of results. Validity is whether a test measures what it is meant to measure; a test can be reliable without being valid.

questions.subject: Assessment of Learning
questions.question: Assessment done during instruction to check progress and give feedback, rather than to grade, is called:
questions.explanation: Formative assessment happens while learning is going on, to guide teaching. Summative assessment comes at the end, to judge what was learned.

questions.subject: Curriculum and Teaching Methods
questions.question: Values and attitudes that learners pick up from school life, though they are not written in any plan, are part of the:
questions.explanation: The hidden curriculum is what learners learn from the school's culture, rules and relationships, without it being planned or written down.

questions.subject: Curriculum and Teaching Methods
questions.question: In Ralph Tyler's model of curriculum development, the first step is:
questions.explanation: Tyler's rationale begins with the purposes the school should seek to attain, then selects and organizes learning experiences, and ends with evaluation.

questions.subject: Curriculum and Teaching Methods
questions.question: At the base of Edgar Dale's Cone of Experience, the most concrete level, are:
questions.explanation: The cone runs from direct, purposeful experiences at the base (most concrete) to verbal symbols at the tip (most abstract).

questions.subject: Curriculum and Teaching Methods
questions.question: The TPACK framework describes the knowledge teachers need to teach well with technology. Besides technological knowledge, it includes:
questions.explanation: TPACK stands for Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge: knowing the technology, how to teach, and the subject, and how the three work together.

questions.subject: The Teaching Profession
questions.question: Which law is the Philippine Teachers Professionalization Act of 1994?
questions.explanation: RA 7836 created the licensure examination for teachers. RA 4670 is the Magna Carta for Public School Teachers, RA 9155 the Governance of Basic Education Act, and RA 10533 the Enhanced Basic Education Act.

questions.subject: The Teaching Profession
questions.question: A parent offers a teacher an expensive gift and asks for a higher grade for their child. Under the Code of Ethics for Professional Teachers, the teacher should:
questions.correct: Decline, because grades must reflect only the learner's performance
wrong: Accept it if the gift is given after grades are released
Accept it and share it with co-teachers
Accept it but give the grade the learner earned
questions.explanation: The Code of Ethics bars teachers from accepting favors or gifts from learners or their parents in exchange for requested concessions. Grades must be based on performance.

questions.subject: The Teaching Profession
questions.question: Which law established the K to 12 basic education program in the Philippines?
questions.explanation: RA 10533, the Enhanced Basic Education Act of 2013, set up K to 12. RA 10931 is the Universal Access to Quality Tertiary Education Act.

questions.subject: The Teaching Profession
questions.question: The lifelong process by which a person learns the norms and values of society, with the family and the school as key agents, is called:
questions.explanation: Socialization is how people learn to take part in society. Social stratification is the ranking of groups in society, and social mobility is movement between those ranks.

questions.subject: Language and Linguistics
questions.question: The smallest unit of meaning in a language is the:
questions.explanation: A morpheme is the smallest unit that carries meaning, such as "un-" or "book". A phoneme is the smallest unit of sound.

questions.subject: Language and Linguistics
questions.question: Which branch of linguistics studies how words combine into phrases and sentences?
questions.explanation: Syntax studies sentence structure. Semantics studies meaning, phonology the sound system, and pragmatics meaning in context.

questions.subject: Language and Linguistics
questions.question: How many morphemes are in the word "unhappiness"?
questions.explanation: "Unhappiness" is made of un- (not) + happy + -ness (state of being): three morphemes.

questions.subject: Literature
questions.question: Who wrote "The Lottery", the short story about a village's yearly ritual?
questions.explanation: "The Lottery" by Shirley Jackson was first published in The New Yorker in 1948.

questions.subject: Literature
questions.question: A poem of 14 lines, traditionally written in iambic pentameter, is a:
questions.explanation: A sonnet has 14 lines, usually in iambic pentameter. A villanelle has 19 lines, a haiku three, and a limerick five.

questions.subject: Literature
questions.question: Who wrote the short story "May Day Eve"?
questions.explanation: "May Day Eve" is by Nick Joaquin, National Artist for Literature. Manuel Arguilla wrote "How My Brother Leon Brought Home a Wife".

questions.subject: Teaching English
questions.question: Which approach develops language mainly through meaningful communication and real-life tasks?
questions.explanation: Communicative Language Teaching puts real communication first. The Grammar-Translation Method focuses on rules and translation, and the Audio-Lingual Method on drills and habit formation.

questions.subject: Teaching English
questions.question: Quickly looking over a text to get its general idea is called:
questions.explanation: Skimming is reading quickly for the main idea. Scanning is searching a text for specific information, such as a date or a name.

questions.subject: Mathematical Concepts and History
questions.question: Who is known as the "Father of Geometry" for organizing geometry into a system of axioms and proofs in the Elements?
questions.explanation: Euclid of Alexandria wrote the Elements (about 300 BCE), which built geometry from definitions, postulates and proofs.

questions.subject: Mathematical Concepts and History
questions.question: The use of zero as a number in its own right, with rules for calculating with it, was first developed by mathematicians in:
questions.explanation: Indian mathematicians such as Brahmagupta (7th century) treated zero as a number and gave rules for arithmetic with it. The idea reached Europe through Arabic texts.

questions.subject: Mathematical Concepts and History
questions.question: The Cartesian coordinate system is named after:
questions.explanation: The name comes from Cartesius, the Latin form of Descartes, who linked algebra and geometry in La Géométrie (1637).

questions.subject: Mathematical Concepts and History
questions.question: Calculus was developed independently in the 17th century by Isaac Newton and:
questions.explanation: Newton and Leibniz developed calculus independently. Much of today's notation, such as dy/dx and the integral sign, comes from Leibniz.

questions.subject: Mathematical Concepts and History
questions.question: How does a mathematical investigation differ from ordinary problem solving?
questions.correct: It is open-ended: learners explore, look for patterns and make conjectures
wrong: It always has one correct answer that the teacher knows in advance
It is limited to routine exercises found in the textbook
It does not require any reasoning or justification of results
questions.explanation: In problem solving the goal is the solution of a given problem. In an investigation the exploration itself is the goal: learners pose questions, find patterns, make and test conjectures.

questions.subject: Mathematical Concepts and History
questions.question: In George Pólya's four-step problem-solving process, the first step is to:
questions.explanation: Pólya's steps in How to Solve It: understand the problem, devise a plan, carry out the plan, and look back.

questions.subject: Mathematical Concepts and History
questions.question: Representing a real situation, such as the growth of a town's population, with an equation that can be studied and tested is called:
questions.explanation: A mathematical model describes a real situation in mathematical terms so it can be analyzed, used for predictions and checked against data.

questions.subject: Problem Solving
questions.question: Solve for x: 3x − 7 = 2x + 5
questions.explanation: Subtract 2x from both sides: x − 7 = 5. Add 7: x = 12.

questions.subject: Problem Solving
questions.question: What are the roots of x² − 5x + 6 = 0?

questions.subject: Problem Solving
questions.question: What is the sum of the roots of 2x² − 8x + 3 = 0?
questions.explanation: For ax² + bx + c = 0, the sum of the roots is −b/a = −(−8)/2 = 4. (The product is c/a = 3/2.)

questions.subject: Problem Solving
questions.question: If log₂ x = 5, what is x?
questions.explanation: log₂ x = 5 means 2⁵ = x, so x = 32.

questions.subject: Problem Solving
questions.question: What is the 20th term of the arithmetic sequence 3, 7, 11, 15, ...?

questions.subject: Problem Solving
questions.question: What is the sum of the first six terms of the geometric series 2 + 6 + 18 + ...?

questions.subject: Problem Solving
questions.question: Ana can paint a room in 6 hours and Ben can paint it in 3 hours. Working together, how long will they take?
questions.explanation: Together they paint 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/2 of the room per hour, so the whole room takes 2 hours.

questions.subject: Problem Solving
questions.question: What is the exact value of sin 30°?
questions.explanation: In a 30°-60°-90° triangle the side opposite 30° is half the hypotenuse, so sin 30° = 1/2.

questions.subject: Problem Solving
questions.question: If tan θ = 3/4 and θ is an acute angle, what is cos θ?
questions.explanation: Take opposite = 3 and adjacent = 4; the hypotenuse is 5. cos θ = adjacent/hypotenuse = 4/5.

questions.subject: Problem Solving
questions.question: A 10-meter ladder leans against a wall and makes a 60° angle with the ground. How high up the wall does it reach?
questions.explanation: Height = 10 sin 60° = 10 × √3/2 = 5√3 m, about 8.66 m.

questions.subject: Problem Solving
questions.question: Simplify (1 − cos²θ) / sin θ, where sin θ ≠ 0.
questions.explanation: Since sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, 1 − cos²θ = sin²θ, and sin²θ / sin θ = sin θ.

questions.subject: Problem Solving
questions.question: What is the sum of the interior angles of a hexagon?

questions.subject: Problem Solving
questions.question: What is the area of a circle with a radius of 7 cm? Use π = 22/7.
questions.explanation: A = πr² = (22/7)(49) = 154 cm². (44 cm is the circumference.)

questions.subject: Problem Solving
questions.question: What is the volume of a sphere with a radius of 3 cm?

questions.subject: Problem Solving
questions.question: The legs of a right triangle are 9 cm and 12 cm. How long is the hypotenuse?

questions.subject: Problem Solving
questions.question: What is the volume of a cylinder with a radius of 2 m and a height of 5 m?
questions.explanation: V = πr²h = π(2²)(5) = 20π m³.

questions.subject: Problem Solving
questions.question: What is the negation of "All teachers are patient"?
questions.explanation: The negation of "all are" is "at least one is not". One impatient teacher is enough to make the original statement false.

questions.subject: Problem Solving
questions.question: If A = {1, 2, 3, 4} and B = {3, 4, 5}, what is A ∩ B?
questions.explanation: The intersection contains the elements in both sets: 3 and 4. {1, 2, 3, 4, 5} is the union.

questions.subject: Problem Solving
questions.question: How many subsets does a set with 4 elements have?
questions.explanation: A set with n elements has 2ⁿ subsets, including the empty set and the set itself: 2⁴ = 16. (15 is the number of proper subsets.)

questions.subject: Problem Solving
questions.question: What is the mean of 4, 8, 6, 10 and 12?

questions.subject: Problem Solving
questions.question: Two fair dice are rolled. What is the probability that the sum is 7?
questions.explanation: Six of the 36 equally likely outcomes give 7: (1,6), (2,5), (3,4), (4,3), (5,2), (6,1). 6/36 = 1/6.

questions.subject: Problem Solving
questions.question: What is the median of 3, 9, 4, 7, 1 and 8?
questions.explanation: In order: 1, 3, 4, 7, 8, 9. With an even number of values, the median is the mean of the two middle ones: (4 + 7)/2 = 5.5.

questions.subject: Problem Solving
questions.question: In how many ways can a committee of 3 be chosen from 7 teachers?
questions.explanation: Order does not matter, so use combinations: C(7, 3) = 7! / (3! × 4!) = 35. (210 counts ordered arrangements.)

questions.subject: Problem Solving
questions.question: What is the slope of the line through (1, 2) and (4, 11)?

questions.subject: Problem Solving
questions.question: What is the distance between the points (−2, 1) and (4, 9)?

questions.subject: Problem Solving
questions.question: What are the center and radius of the circle x² + y² − 6x + 4y − 12 = 0?
questions.explanation: Complete the squares: (x − 3)² + (y + 2)² = 12 + 9 + 4 = 25. The center is (3, −2) and the radius is √25 = 5.

questions.subject: Problem Solving
questions.question: What is the derivative of f(x) = 3x⁴ − 2x + 7?
questions.explanation: By the power rule, d/dx(3x⁴) = 12x³, d/dx(−2x) = −2, and the derivative of a constant is 0.

questions.subject: Problem Solving
questions.question: Evaluate the limit of (x² − 4) / (x − 2) as x approaches 2.
questions.explanation: For x ≠ 2, (x² − 4)/(x − 2) = (x + 2)(x − 2)/(x − 2) = x + 2, which approaches 4.

questions.subject: Problem Solving
questions.question: Evaluate the definite integral of 3x² from x = 0 to x = 2.
questions.explanation: An antiderivative of 3x² is x³. So the integral is 2³ − 0³ = 8.

questions.subject: Problem Solving
questions.question: What is the greatest common factor of 84 and 126?
questions.explanation: 84 = 2² × 3 × 7 and 126 = 2 × 3² × 7. The common factors are 2 × 3 × 7 = 42. (252 is the least common multiple.)

questions.subject: Problem Solving
questions.question: How much simple interest does ₱10,000 earn at 6% a year for 3 years?
questions.explanation: I = Prt = 10,000 × 0.06 × 3 = ₱1,800. (₱1,910.16 would be the interest if it were compounded annually.)

questions.subject: Problem Solving
questions.question: What does ₱5,000 grow to in 2 years at 10% interest compounded annually?
questions.explanation: A = P(1 + r)ᵗ = 5,000 × 1.1² = 5,000 × 1.21 = ₱6,050. Simple interest would give ₱6,000.

questions.subject: Teaching Mathematics
questions.question: In the concrete–pictorial–abstract (CPA) approach, what comes after learners work with real objects?
questions.correct: Pictures and diagrams of the objects
wrong: Symbols and equations for the operation
A summative test on the concept
questions.explanation: CPA moves from handling objects (concrete) to drawings and diagrams (pictorial) to numbers and symbols (abstract).

questions.subject: Teaching Mathematics
questions.question: A student writes (a + b)² = a² + b². What is the best way to address this error?
questions.correct: Show the area of a square with side a + b to reveal the missing 2ab
wrong: Mark it wrong and move on to the next topic quickly
Tell the student to memorize the correct formula by heart
Give more drill items on squaring without discussing the error
questions.explanation: An area model makes the two a × b rectangles visible, so the student understands why (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b² instead of memorizing a rule.

questions.subject: Teaching Mathematics
questions.question: Which is an example of formative assessment in a mathematics class?
questions.correct: An exit slip with two problems at the end of the lesson
wrong: The quarterly examination given at the end of the term
A standardized test given at the end of the school year
The final grade written on the learner's report card
questions.explanation: Formative assessment happens during learning and is used to adjust teaching. The other choices judge learning after it is finished.

questions.subject: Teaching Mathematics
questions.question: In the van Hiele model of geometric thinking, a learner who recognizes shapes only by their overall appearance is at which level?
questions.explanation: At the visualization level, a square is a square because it "looks like one". At the analysis level, learners describe shapes by their properties.

questions.subject: Teaching Mathematics
questions.question: In a spiral curriculum such as K to 12 mathematics, topics are:
questions.correct: Revisited across grade levels with increasing depth
wrong: Arranged by difficulty within a single grade only
Chosen freely by each teacher every year
questions.explanation: Following Bruner, a spiral curriculum returns to key ideas in later grades, each time at a higher level, building on what was learned before.

questions.subject: Teaching Mathematics
questions.question: Which tool best lets students explore how changing m and b moves the graph of y = mx + b?
questions.correct: Dynamic graphing software such as GeoGebra
wrong: A slide presentation with fixed images
questions.explanation: Dynamic software lets students change m and b and see the graph move at once, so they can discover the effect of slope and y-intercept.

questions.subject: Teaching Mathematics
questions.question: A teacher tries a new strategy in her own class, measures its effect on scores, and uses the results to improve her teaching. This is:
questions.explanation: Action research is done by teachers in their own classrooms to solve a practical problem and improve their practice.

questions.subject: Teaching Mathematics
questions.question: Students list all possible outcomes of a situation in a systematic table before answering. Which problem-solving strategy are they using?
questions.explanation: Making an organized list helps learners count every case without missing or repeating any.

questions.subject: Teaching Mathematics
questions.question: To score students' written solutions separately on understanding, strategy and final answer, the most suitable tool is:
questions.explanation: An analytic rubric scores each criterion on its own, so the teacher and the student see which part of the solution needs work.

questions.subject: Teaching Mathematics
questions.question: A learner says 0.25 is greater than 0.5 because 25 is greater than 5. This shows a misconception about:
questions.explanation: The learner treats the digits after the point as a whole number. In fact 0.5 = 0.50, which is greater than 0.25.

questions.subject: Teaching Mathematics
questions.question: Which activity best connects percent to learners' daily lives?
questions.correct: Computing the sale prices of items in a store flyer with discounts
wrong: Memorizing the definition of percent and its symbol
Copying percent problems from the board into notebooks
Converting a list of fractions to percents
questions.explanation: Using real discounts shows learners why percent matters and gives them a meaningful context to apply it.

questions.subject: The Teaching Profession
questions.question: A teacher believes that learners learn best by doing and by solving real problems, and that school should be like life itself. This view reflects:
questions.explanation: Pragmatism, associated with John Dewey, holds that learning comes from experience and problem solving, and that education is life, not only preparation for it.

questions.subject: The Teaching Profession
questions.question: A school focuses on a core of basic knowledge and skills such as reading, writing and arithmetic, with the teacher leading and learners expected to master them. This reflects:
questions.explanation: Essentialism stresses a common core of essential knowledge and skills, taught systematically by the teacher, with an emphasis on mastery and discipline.

questions.subject: The Teaching Profession
questions.question: A teacher lets learners choose their own projects and stresses that each person must find meaning and take responsibility for his or her choices. This reflects:
questions.explanation: Existentialism emphasizes individual freedom, personal choice and responsibility; learners create their own meaning.

questions.subject: The Teaching Profession
questions.question: Which law institutionalizes inclusive education and support services for learners with disabilities in the Philippines?
questions.explanation: RA 11650 (2022) sets a policy of inclusion and services for learners with disabilities. RA 10157 is the Kindergarten Education Act, RA 9155 the Governance of Basic Education Act, and RA 10931 the free tertiary education law.

questions.subject: The Teaching Profession
questions.question: A learner keeps talking during class. Under the Code of Ethics for Professional Teachers, which of these may the teacher NOT do?
questions.correct: Lower the learner's grade as a punishment for talking
wrong: Talk with the learner privately about the behavior
Inform the learner's parents about the behavior
Apply the class rules that the learners agreed on
questions.explanation: The Code of Ethics says a teacher shall not make deductions from a learner's scholastic ratings as punishment for acts that are not signs of poor scholarship. Grades must reflect learning.

questions.subject: The Teaching Profession
questions.question: Which law, known as the Magna Carta for Public School Teachers, sets the working conditions and benefits of public school teachers, such as hours of work and leave?
questions.explanation: RA 4670 (1966) is the Magna Carta for Public School Teachers. RA 7836 is the Teachers Professionalization Act, which created the licensure examination.

questions.subject: Curriculum and Teaching Methods
questions.question: Which curriculum model is called the "grassroots approach" because it holds that the teachers who teach the learners should design the curriculum?
wrong: Galen Saylor and William Alexander's model
questions.explanation: Hilda Taba argued that curriculum should be built from the bottom up by teachers, starting with teaching-learning units for their own learners.

questions.subject: Curriculum and Teaching Methods
questions.question: The curriculum proposed by scholars and professional organizations as what schools ought to teach is called the:
questions.explanation: In Glatthorn's types of curriculum, the recommended curriculum comes from experts and organizations. The written curriculum is the documented plan a school adopts from it.

questions.subject: Curriculum and Teaching Methods
questions.question: Textbooks, laboratory equipment, computers and the time given to a subject are part of the:
questions.explanation: The supported curriculum is the set of resources that help teachers deliver the curriculum: materials, equipment, facilities and time.

questions.subject: Curriculum and Teaching Methods
questions.question: In Understanding by Design (backward design), the first stage is to:
questions.explanation: Wiggins and McTighe's backward design starts with the desired results, then decides on the evidence of learning, and only then plans the learning activities.

questions.subject: Curriculum and Teaching Methods
questions.question: Making sure that intended learning outcomes, teaching activities and assessment tasks all match one another is called:
questions.explanation: John Biggs' constructive alignment links outcomes, teaching and assessment, so learners are taught and assessed on exactly what they are meant to learn.

questions.subject: Curriculum and Teaching Methods
questions.question: Each member of a group studies one part of a topic, discusses it with members from other groups who studied the same part, then teaches it to the home group. This strategy is called:
questions.explanation: In the jigsaw strategy every member becomes an "expert" on one piece and is responsible for teaching it, so the group needs everyone's part.

questions.subject: Curriculum and Teaching Methods
questions.question: Learners are given materials and guiding questions so that they find the rule or concept by themselves. This is the:
questions.explanation: In the discovery approach (associated with Jerome Bruner) learners explore and arrive at the concept themselves, with the teacher guiding.

questions.subject: Curriculum and Teaching Methods
questions.question: Why should a teacher wait three to five seconds after asking a question before calling on a learner?
questions.correct: Learners get time to think, so more of them give better answers
wrong: It saves class time by letting the fastest learners answer first
It gives the teacher time to check attendance quietly
It makes learners anxious, which keeps them more alert
questions.explanation: Research on "wait time" (Mary Budd Rowe) found that longer pauses lead to longer, more thoughtful answers and more learners responding.

questions.subject: Curriculum and Teaching Methods
questions.question: Which learning objective is stated in measurable terms?
questions.correct: Given five fractions, the learners will order them from least to greatest with 80% accuracy
wrong: The learners will understand how to arrange fractions from least to greatest
The learners will appreciate the value of fractions in daily life
The learners will know the steps for comparing and ordering fractions
questions.explanation: A measurable objective names an observable behavior (arrange), the condition (given five fractions) and the standard (80% accuracy). "Understand", "appreciate" and "know" cannot be observed directly.

questions.subject: Curriculum and Teaching Methods
questions.question: Teaching learners to check the source, date and evidence of a news post before sharing it develops:
questions.explanation: Media and information literacy is the ability to find, evaluate and use information responsibly, including spotting false or misleading content.

questions.subject: Curriculum and Teaching Methods
questions.question: A lesson in which learners make a weekly budget from their allowance develops:
questions.explanation: Financial literacy covers managing money: budgeting, saving, spending wisely and understanding basic financial concepts.

questions.subject: Curriculum and Teaching Methods
questions.question: Learners type an essay in a word processor instead of writing it by hand, and nothing else about the task changes. In the SAMR model, this is:
questions.explanation: In Puentedura's SAMR model, substitution means technology replaces a tool with no functional change. Augmentation adds improvements, such as spell check used as part of the task.

questions.subject: Curriculum and Teaching Methods
questions.question: In the ASSURE model for planning lessons that use media and technology, the first step is to:
wrong: Select strategies, technology, media and materials
questions.explanation: ASSURE stands for Analyze learners, State standards and objectives, Select strategies and materials, Utilize them, Require learner participation, and Evaluate and revise.

questions.subject: Curriculum and Teaching Methods
questions.question: DepEd's Indigenous Peoples Education (IPEd) program mainly aims to:
questions.correct: Make education responsive to indigenous communities' cultures, languages and knowledge
wrong: Replace indigenous languages with English and Filipino as early as possible
Teach indigenous learners the national curriculum only, without local content
Move indigenous learners to larger schools outside their communities
questions.explanation: IPEd (DepEd Order No. 62, s. 2011) calls for education that respects and uses indigenous peoples' culture, language and knowledge systems.

questions.subject: Child and Adolescent Learners
questions.question: A learner follows rules only to avoid being punished. In Kohlberg's theory, this learner is at the:
questions.explanation: At Kohlberg's preconventional level, moral reasoning is based on avoiding punishment and getting rewards. "Formal operational" is a Piaget stage, not a Kohlberg level.

questions.subject: Child and Adolescent Learners
questions.question: A learner behaves well mainly to be seen as a "good person" and to please parents and teachers. In Kohlberg's theory, this is the:
questions.explanation: The conventional level is about meeting others' expectations and following social rules ("good boy/good girl", then law and order).

questions.subject: Child and Adolescent Learners
questions.question: A learner understands best through movement, building models and hands-on activities. In Gardner's theory, this shows strength in:
questions.explanation: Bodily-kinesthetic intelligence is the ability to use the body skillfully and to learn through physical activity.

questions.subject: Child and Adolescent Learners
questions.question: In Bronfenbrenner's ecological systems theory, a child's family, classmates and teachers belong to the:
questions.explanation: The microsystem is the child's immediate surroundings with direct contact. The mesosystem is the links between them, such as parent-teacher relations.

questions.subject: Child and Adolescent Learners
questions.question: A learner who comes to school hungry cannot focus on the lesson. According to Maslow, which need must be met first?
questions.explanation: Maslow placed physiological needs such as food and rest at the base of the hierarchy; higher needs, including learning, are hard to pursue while they are unmet.

questions.subject: Child and Adolescent Learners
questions.question: Learners may show what they learned by making a poster, writing an essay or recording a short talk. This is differentiation by:
questions.explanation: In Tomlinson's model, teachers can differentiate content (what is learned), process (how), product (how learning is shown) and the learning environment.

questions.subject: Child and Adolescent Learners
questions.question: Learners start writing neatly after seeing a classmate praised for neat work. This is explained by:
questions.explanation: Albert Bandura's social learning theory holds that people learn by observing others and the consequences of their behavior.

questions.subject: Child and Adolescent Learners
questions.question: A child calls every four-legged animal "dog", then learns that cats are different and forms a new category for them. This shows:
questions.explanation: In Piaget's terms, fitting new things into an existing schema is assimilation; changing the schema or creating a new one, as here, is accommodation.

questions.subject: Child and Adolescent Learners
questions.question: Asking learners "How did you get your answer, and what would you do differently next time?" develops:
questions.explanation: Metacognition is thinking about one's own thinking: planning, monitoring and evaluating how one learns and solves problems.

questions.subject: Assessment of Learning
questions.question: A mathematics test uses long, difficult reading passages, so poor readers fail even when they know the math. This mainly threatens the test's:
questions.explanation: Validity is whether a test measures what it is meant to measure. Here reading ability interferes with measuring mathematics.

questions.subject: Assessment of Learning
questions.question: In item analysis, an item answered correctly by 90% of the examinees is considered:
questions.explanation: The difficulty index is the proportion of examinees who answer correctly. A value of 0.90 means the item is easy.

questions.subject: Assessment of Learning
questions.question: More low-scoring than high-scoring examinees answered an item correctly. Its discrimination index is:
questions.correct: Negative, so the item should be revised or discarded
wrong: Zero, so the item discriminates well and should be kept
Positive, so the item should be kept as it is
Above 1.0, which means the item is excellent
questions.explanation: A negative discrimination index means the item favors low scorers, often because of a wrong key or confusing wording. The index ranges from −1 to +1.

questions.subject: Assessment of Learning
questions.question: In a normal distribution, about what percentage of scores fall within one standard deviation of the mean?
questions.explanation: By the empirical rule, about 68% of scores lie within 1 SD of the mean, 95% within 2 SD, and 99.7% within 3 SD.

questions.subject: Assessment of Learning
questions.question: On a very difficult test, most learners got low scores and only a few got high scores. The score distribution is:
questions.explanation: When scores pile up at the low end with a tail toward the high scores, the distribution is positively (right) skewed.

questions.subject: Assessment of Learning
questions.question: Which is an example of authentic assessment?
questions.correct: Learners plan and cook a balanced meal and explain their choices
wrong: A multiple-choice test on the food groups and their examples
A true-or-false quiz on the nutrients found in common foods
A matching test pairing common foods with their vitamins
questions.explanation: Authentic assessment asks learners to apply knowledge and skills to a real-life task, not only recall facts.

questions.subject: Assessment of Learning
questions.question: A test that compares each learner's score with the scores of other learners is:
questions.explanation: A norm-referenced test ranks learners against one another. A criterion-referenced test compares each learner with a set standard or objective.

questions.subject: Assessment of Learning
questions.question: A rubric that gives a single overall score for the whole performance is a:
questions.explanation: A holistic rubric judges the performance as a whole. An analytic rubric scores each criterion separately.

questions.subject: Field Study and Action Research
questions.question: In field study courses, pre-service teachers mainly:
questions.correct: Observe and assist in real classes to link theory with practice
wrong: Teach full classes alone, without a cooperating teacher
Study teaching theories from textbooks, away from schools
Help with the school's records and administrative work
questions.explanation: Field study gives pre-service teachers guided experience in actual schools, so they can see how the theories they studied work in real classrooms.

questions.subject: Field Study and Action Research
questions.question: During teaching internship, the cooperating teacher's main role is to:
questions.correct: Mentor the pre-service teacher, model good teaching and give feedback
wrong: Let the pre-service teacher grade all the learners alone
Leave the class entirely to the pre-service teacher from the first day
Check only the pre-service teacher's attendance
questions.explanation: The cooperating teacher guides the intern step by step, demonstrates good practice, observes lessons and gives feedback for improvement.

questions.subject: Field Study and Action Research
questions.question: A teaching portfolio is best described as:
questions.correct: Selected work and reflections that show growth as a teacher
wrong: A complete record of the teacher's daily attendance and leaves
A file of lesson plans copied from published teaching guides
A single final examination taken at the end of the program
questions.explanation: A portfolio gathers selected evidence such as lesson plans, learners' work, observations and reflections to show learning and development over time.

questions.subject: Field Study and Action Research
questions.question: After each lesson, a teacher writes down what worked, what did not, and what to change next time. This practice is called:
questions.explanation: Reflective teaching means looking back on one's teaching to understand it and improve it, a habit stressed throughout field study and internship.

questions.subject: Field Study and Action Research
questions.question: Teaching a short lesson to a small group of peers, focusing on one skill and followed by feedback, is called:
questions.explanation: Microteaching scales teaching down in time, class size and scope so pre-service teachers can practice and refine specific skills.

questions.subject: Field Study and Action Research
questions.question: An observer writes a brief, factual account of a specific incident involving a learner, without judging it. This tool is:
questions.explanation: An anecdotal record describes what happened objectively and in detail; interpretation, if any, is kept separate.

questions.subject: Field Study and Action Research
questions.question: While observing, a pre-service teacher notes how the teacher gets the class's attention, gives instructions and handles transitions. The focus of this observation is:
questions.explanation: Getting attention, giving instructions and managing transitions are classroom management routines that keep learning time productive.

questions.subject: Field Study and Action Research
questions.question: Arranging seats in small groups, posting class rules made with the learners and displaying their work mainly builds:
wrong: A strictly teacher-centered and controlled setting
A formal environment designed mainly for testing
An efficient routine for administrative tasks
questions.explanation: Shared rules, group seating and displayed work give learners ownership and support collaboration and motivation.

questions.subject: Field Study and Action Research
questions.question: The first step in doing classroom action research is to:
questions.correct: Identify a problem in one's own classroom
wrong: Choose a sample from other schools
questions.explanation: Action research starts from a real problem the teacher faces, such as low reading scores, then plans and tries a solution and studies the results.

questions.subject: Field Study and Action Research
questions.question: The main purpose of classroom action research is to:
questions.correct: Improve teaching and learning in the researcher's own setting
wrong: Prove a theory that applies to all schools everywhere
Compare the school's results with national test scores
Evaluate the performance of other teachers in the school
questions.explanation: Action research is practical and local: teachers study their own practice to make it better for their own learners.

questions.subject: Field Study and Action Research
questions.question: Before including learners' work in an action research report, the teacher should:
questions.correct: Get consent and keep the learners' identities confidential
wrong: Publish their full names so they get credit for their work
Ask only the principal's opinion before using the work
Use the work freely, since it was made in the teacher's class
questions.explanation: Ethical research protects participants: informed consent (from parents for minors) and confidentiality are basic requirements.

questions.subject: Field Study and Action Research
questions.question: In action research, giving learners the same kind of test before and after an intervention to see whether scores improved is a:
wrong: Case study of one school building
questions.explanation: Comparing pretest and posttest results shows whether learners improved after the intervention, a common design in classroom action research.

questions.subject: Field Study and Action Research
questions.question: In Kemmis and McTaggart's action research spiral, which step comes after observing?
questions.explanation: The cycle is plan, act, observe, reflect. Reflection then leads into a revised plan for the next cycle.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which sentence is written in the active voice?
questions.correct: The committee approved the new policy.
wrong: The new policy was approved by the committee.
Approval was given to the new policy.
questions.explanation: In the active voice the subject does the action: the committee (subject) approved (verb) the policy. In the others the policy receives the action.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Each of the students ___ a laptop for the online class.
questions.explanation: "Each" is singular, so it takes a singular verb: "Each of the students has." The phrase "of the students" does not change the subject.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: In the communication process, the receiver's response to the message is called:
questions.explanation: Feedback is the receiver's reaction that tells the sender how the message was understood. Encoding is putting ideas into words; noise is anything that disrupts the message.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The speaker's argument was so cogent that even her critics agreed with it. "Cogent" means:
questions.explanation: A cogent argument is clear, logical and persuasive. The context, even her critics agreed, points to convincing.

questions.subject: Filipino
questions.question: Alin ang wastong salita sa patlang: "Pumunta siya ___ palengke kaninang umaga."
questions.explanation: Ginagamit ang "sa" bilang pang-ukol na tumutukoy sa lugar o direksyon. Ang "kay" ay ginagamit sa pangalan ng tao.

questions.subject: Filipino
questions.question: Alin ang pangungusap na wasto ang gamit ng "ng" o "nang"?
questions.explanation: Ginagamit ang "nang" bago ang pang-abay na pamaraan na naglalarawan kung paano ginawa ang kilos, gaya ng "nang mabilis". Ang "ng" ay pantukoy o pang-ukol bago ang pangngalan.

questions.subject: Filipino
questions.question: Anong uri ng tayutay ang "Ang kanyang puso ay bato"?
questions.explanation: Ang pagwawangis (metapora) ay tuwirang paghahambing nang hindi gumagamit ng "tulad ng" o "parang". Ang pagtutulad (simile) ay gumagamit ng mga salitang ito.

questions.subject: Science and Technology
questions.question: What is the SI unit of electric current?
questions.explanation: Electric current is measured in amperes. The volt measures potential difference, the ohm resistance, and the watt power.

questions.subject: Science and Technology
questions.question: Which layer of the atmosphere contains the ozone layer that absorbs most of the Sun's ultraviolet radiation?
questions.explanation: The ozone layer lies in the stratosphere, above the troposphere where weather happens.

questions.subject: Science and Technology
questions.question: Which is the best example of technology used to reduce disaster risk in the Philippines?
questions.correct: Emergency text alerts sent to phones before a typhoon makes landfall
wrong: Online games that learners play during class suspensions
Shopping apps used to order goods for home delivery
Video streaming services showing typhoon documentaries
questions.explanation: Early-warning systems such as emergency cell broadcasts give people time to evacuate and prepare, reducing loss of life.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The price of a shirt went up from ₱400 to ₱500. What is the percent increase?
questions.explanation: Percent increase = (500 − 400) / 400 × 100 = 25%. The increase is compared with the original price, not the new one (which would give 20%).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Five workers can build a fence in 12 days. How many days would six workers take, working at the same rate?
questions.explanation: The job takes 5 × 12 = 60 worker-days. Six workers need 60 / 6 = 10 days. More workers means fewer days (inverse variation).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Simplify: 2 + 3 × (8 − 5)²
questions.explanation: Parentheses first: 8 − 5 = 3. Then the exponent: 3² = 9. Then multiplication: 3 × 9 = 27. Finally addition: 2 + 27 = 29.

questions.subject: Philippine History
questions.question: Who led the local forces that defeated Ferdinand Magellan in the Battle of Mactan in 1521?
questions.explanation: Lapulapu, chieftain of Mactan, led the fighters who defeated Magellan's men on April 27, 1521. Rajah Humabon of Cebu had allied with Magellan.

questions.subject: Philippine History
questions.question: Philippine independence from Spain was proclaimed on June 12, 1898 in:
questions.explanation: Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed independence from the window of his house in Kawit, Cavite. Malolos was where the First Republic's constitution was drafted.

questions.subject: Philippine History
questions.question: The First Philippine Republic, also called the Malolos Republic, was inaugurated in:
questions.explanation: The Malolos Republic was inaugurated on January 23, 1899, with Emilio Aguinaldo as President, after the Malolos Constitution was approved.

questions.subject: Philippine History
questions.question: In what year was the Commonwealth of the Philippines inaugurated, with Manuel L. Quezon as President?
questions.explanation: The Commonwealth was inaugurated on November 15, 1935, as a ten-year transition to full independence.

questions.subject: Philippine History
questions.question: The Philippines gained independence from the United States on July 4, 1946. Who became the first President of the Third Republic?
questions.explanation: Manuel Roxas, the last Commonwealth President, became the first President of the independent Third Republic in 1946.

questions.subject: Philippine History
questions.question: The 1986 People Power Revolution that ended the Marcos regime took place mainly along:
questions.correct: EDSA, Epifanio de los Santos Avenue
questions.explanation: In February 1986, millions gathered peacefully along EDSA, leading to the end of Ferdinand Marcos' rule and Corazon Aquino becoming President.

questions.subject: Philippine History
questions.question: Which is a primary source about the Battle of Mactan?
questions.correct: Pigafetta's account, written during Magellan's voyage
wrong: A history textbook on Magellan published in 2015
An encyclopedia article on Magellan's expedition
A documentary film about Lapulapu made in 2021
questions.explanation: A primary source comes from the time of the event, usually from a witness. Pigafetta sailed with Magellan and wrote down what he saw.

questions.subject: Life and Works of Rizal
questions.question: José Rizal was executed on December 30, 1896 at:
questions.explanation: Rizal was shot at Bagumbayan, now Rizal Park (Luneta). He had been held at Fort Santiago before his execution.

questions.subject: Life and Works of Rizal
questions.question: Where was Rizal exiled from 1892 to 1896, where he ran a school for boys and practiced medicine?
questions.explanation: The Spanish authorities exiled Rizal to Dapitan in Mindanao, where he also did farming, engineering and community projects.

questions.subject: Life and Works of Rizal
questions.question: Rizal founded La Liga Filipina in 1892 mainly to:
questions.correct: Unite Filipinos and work for reforms through peaceful means
wrong: Start an armed revolution against Spanish rule
Publish La Solidaridad from Barcelona and Madrid
Train soldiers and raise funds for the Katipunan
questions.explanation: La Liga Filipina was a civic organization for unity, mutual help and peaceful reform. Rizal was arrested and exiled days after founding it.

questions.subject: Life and Works of Rizal
questions.question: Which law requires the teaching of Rizal's life, works and writings, especially Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo, in all schools?
questions.explanation: RA 1425 (1956), the Rizal Law, was sponsored by Senator Claro M. Recto and Senator Jose P. Laurel.

questions.subject: Life and Works of Rizal
questions.question: Rizal's farewell poem, later titled "Mi Último Adiós", mainly expresses:
questions.correct: His love for the Philippines and his readiness to die for it
wrong: His anger at the friars and officials who condemned him
A call for Filipinos to take up arms immediately
His regret for writing the two novels that led to his death
questions.explanation: Written in his last days in Fort Santiago, the poem bids farewell to his beloved country and offers his life for it.

questions.subject: Ethics
questions.question: According to Immanuel Kant, an act is morally right when:
questions.correct: It is done out of duty and its rule could apply to everyone
wrong: It produces the greatest happiness for the most people
It is approved by most people in one's community
It brings the greatest benefit to the one who acts
questions.explanation: Kant's categorical imperative: act only on a rule you could will to be a universal law. Results such as happiness do not make an act right.

questions.subject: Ethics
questions.question: Choosing the action that brings the greatest good to the greatest number of people reflects:
questions.explanation: Utilitarianism, developed by Jeremy Bentham and John Stuart Mill, judges actions by their consequences for overall happiness.

questions.subject: Ethics
questions.question: In Aristotle's virtue ethics, courage is the mean between:
questions.explanation: For Aristotle, a virtue lies between two extremes: too little (deficiency) and too much (excess). Courage lies between cowardice and rashness.

questions.subject: Ethics
questions.question: A situation in which a person must choose between two options, each of which breaks a moral principle, is a:
questions.explanation: In a moral dilemma no option is free of moral cost, so the person must weigh competing principles.

questions.subject: Ethics
questions.question: The Filipino value of feeling a lasting duty to repay a kindness is called:
questions.explanation: Utang na loob is a debt of gratitude. Pakikisama is getting along with others, and hiya is a sense of shame or propriety.

questions.subject: The Contemporary World
questions.question: Globalization is best described as:
questions.correct: The growing interconnection of economies, cultures and peoples worldwide
wrong: The withdrawal of countries from world trade, travel and exchange
The rule of one powerful country over all other countries
The use of only locally made products in every country
questions.explanation: Globalization links countries through trade, investment, migration, technology and the spread of ideas and culture.

questions.subject: The Contemporary World
questions.question: The Philippines is a founding member of which regional organization established in 1967?
questions.explanation: The Association of Southeast Asian Nations was founded in Bangkok on August 8, 1967, by Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore and Thailand.

questions.subject: The Contemporary World
questions.question: Money that overseas Filipino workers send home to their families is called:
questions.explanation: Remittances from overseas Filipinos are a major source of income for many families and an important part of the Philippine economy.

questions.subject: The Contemporary World
questions.question: The United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) are meant to be achieved by the year:
questions.explanation: The 17 SDGs were adopted in 2015 as part of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.

questions.subject: The Contemporary World
questions.question: The Paris Agreement on climate change mainly aims to:
questions.correct: Limit global warming to well below 2°C above pre-industrial levels
wrong: Ban all use of fossil fuels worldwide by the year 2020
Require every country to cut emissions by exactly half
Create a world government to manage the climate
questions.explanation: Adopted in 2015, the Paris Agreement aims to keep warming well below 2°C and to pursue efforts to limit it to 1.5°C.

questions.subject: The Contemporary World
questions.question: Glocalization means:
questions.correct: Adapting global products or ideas to fit local cultures
wrong: Rejecting foreign products to protect local culture
Making the cultures of all countries the same
Moving factories to countries with cheaper labor
questions.explanation: An example is an international fast-food chain adding local dishes, such as rice meals, to its menu in the Philippines.

questions.subject: The Contemporary World
questions.question: Which international organization deals with the rules of trade between nations?
questions.explanation: The WTO handles global trade rules and trade disputes. The IMF works on monetary cooperation and financial stability.

questions.subject: Art Appreciation
questions.question: Who painted the "Spoliarium", which won a gold medal at the Madrid Exposition of Fine Arts in 1884?
questions.explanation: Juan Luna's Spoliarium won a gold medal in 1884; Félix Resurrección Hidalgo won a silver medal at the same exposition.

questions.subject: Art Appreciation
questions.question: Fernando Amorsolo, the first National Artist, is best known for paintings of:
questions.correct: Sunlit rural scenes, often with a glowing backlight
wrong: Abstract geometric shapes in bold primary colors
Dark religious murals in old Spanish churches
Cubist portraits of city people and workers
questions.explanation: In 1972 Amorsolo became the very first National Artist of the Philippines, for painting (visual arts), conferred shortly after his death. He painted bright countryside scenes, such as rice planting, known for his backlighting technique.

questions.subject: Art Appreciation
questions.question: In art, the lightness or darkness of a color is called its:
questions.explanation: Value describes how light or dark a color is. Hue is the name of the color itself, such as red or blue.

questions.subject: Art Appreciation
questions.question: Repeating shapes, lines or colors to create a sense of movement in an artwork uses the principle of:
questions.explanation: Rhythm is created by repetition of elements, which leads the eye across the work. Emphasis makes one part stand out.

questions.subject: Art Appreciation
questions.question: Art that does not try to show real objects, and uses shapes, colors and lines for their own sake, is called:
questions.explanation: Abstract (non-representational) art expresses ideas or feelings through form and color rather than recognizable subjects.

questions.subject: Art Appreciation
questions.question: The Maranao decorative art with flowing, curving and leaf-like designs, seen in wood carving and brass, is called:
questions.explanation: Okir is the curvilinear ornamental design of the Maranao and other Muslim groups in Mindanao. Tinikling is a dance, kundiman a song form, and zarzuela a musical play.

questions.subject: Art Appreciation
questions.question: A poster that encourages citizens to register and vote mainly serves which function of art?
questions.explanation: Art has a social function when it influences group behavior or addresses public issues. A physical function refers to useful objects, such as chairs or buildings.

questions.subject: Understanding the Self
questions.question: Which philosopher is associated with the saying that "the unexamined life is not worth living"?
questions.explanation: Socrates taught that wisdom begins with knowing oneself and urged people to examine their lives and beliefs.

questions.subject: Understanding the Self
questions.question: Who said "I think, therefore I am"?
questions.explanation: Descartes' "Cogito, ergo sum" holds that the one thing a person cannot doubt is his or her own existence as a thinking being.

questions.subject: Understanding the Self
questions.question: According to William James, the clothes, possessions and family that a person considers part of who he or she is make up the:
questions.explanation: James divided the self into the material self (body, possessions, family), the social self (how others see us), and the spiritual self (inner thoughts and values).

questions.subject: Understanding the Self
questions.question: In Carl Rogers' theory, a large gap between a person's real self and ideal self results in:
questions.explanation: Rogers held that when the real self and ideal self differ greatly, a person experiences incongruence, which can cause anxiety. Closeness between them is congruence.

questions.subject: Understanding the Self
questions.question: John Locke described the mind at birth as a "tabula rasa", meaning:
questions.correct: A blank slate that is filled in by experience
wrong: A mind already filled with inborn ideas
A soul that exists apart from the body
A mirror that reflects the mind of God
questions.explanation: Locke argued that people are born without built-in ideas and that the self is formed through experience and memory.

questions.subject: Understanding the Self
questions.question: Posting only one's best moments online, so that one's online image differs from real life, relates most to the:
questions.explanation: The digital self is the identity a person presents online, which can be curated and may differ from the offline self.

questions.subject: Language and Linguistics
questions.question: "Ship" and "sheep" differ in only one sound, which changes the meaning. Such pairs of words are called:
questions.explanation: A minimal pair differs in one sound in the same position, which shows that the two sounds are separate phonemes (here /ɪ/ and /iː/).

questions.subject: Language and Linguistics
questions.question: The /p/ in "pin" is pronounced with a puff of air, but the /p/ in "spin" is not. These different forms of the same phoneme are called:
questions.explanation: Allophones are variants of one phoneme that do not change meaning. Aspirated [pʰ] and unaspirated [p] are allophones of /p/ in English.

questions.subject: Language and Linguistics
questions.question: Studying how "Can you pass the salt?" is understood as a request and not as a question about ability belongs to:
questions.explanation: Pragmatics studies meaning in context: what speakers intend beyond the literal words.

questions.subject: Language and Linguistics
questions.question: The branch of linguistics that studies the meaning of words and sentences is:
questions.explanation: Semantics deals with meaning, including word meaning and relations such as synonymy and antonymy. Syntax deals with sentence structure.

questions.subject: Language and Linguistics
questions.question: In the word "replay", the prefix "re-" is a:
questions.explanation: A bound morpheme cannot stand alone as a word; it must attach to another morpheme. "Play" is a free morpheme.

questions.subject: Language and Linguistics
questions.question: Which of these suffixes is inflectional?
questions.explanation: Inflectional suffixes mark grammar, such as plural "-s", without changing the word class. "-ness", "-ful" and agentive "-er" are derivational: they form new words.

questions.subject: Language and Linguistics
questions.question: In Krashen's theory, language is acquired through understandable input that is a little beyond the learner's current level. This is called the:
questions.explanation: Krashen's input hypothesis says acquisition happens when learners understand input slightly above their level, written as i + 1.

questions.subject: Language and Linguistics
questions.question: A learner who is anxious and afraid of making mistakes takes in less of the language he hears. Krashen explains this with the:
questions.explanation: The affective filter is an emotional barrier: high anxiety and low motivation block input from being acquired, so a relaxed classroom helps.

questions.subject: Language and Linguistics
questions.question: A speaker moves between English and Filipino within one conversation, as in "Let's go na, late na tayo." This is called:
questions.explanation: Code-switching is alternating between two or more languages in one conversation. A pidgin is a simplified contact language; a creole is a pidgin that has become a first language.

questions.subject: Language and Linguistics
questions.question: Under the 1987 Policy on Bilingual Education (DECS Order No. 52, s. 1987), which two languages were designated as the media of instruction?
wrong: English and the regional language only
questions.explanation: The 1987 policy used Filipino and English as media of instruction for different learning areas. The earlier 1974 policy had named Pilipino and English. Language-in-education policy later changed under the K to 12 program.

questions.subject: Language and Linguistics
questions.question: "Although it rained, the program continued." What kind of sentence is this?
questions.explanation: It has one independent clause (the program continued) and one dependent clause (although it rained), which makes it a complex sentence.

questions.subject: Literature
questions.question: "Biag ni Lam-ang" is an epic of the:
questions.explanation: Biag ni Lam-ang is the Ilocano epic of the hero Lam-ang. The Ifugao have the Hudhud, the Maranao the Darangen, and the people of Panay the Hinilawod.

questions.subject: Literature
questions.question: The Hudhud, chanted during rice harvesting and funerals and recognized by UNESCO, belongs to the:
questions.explanation: The Hudhud chants of the Ifugao were proclaimed a Masterpiece of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity by UNESCO in 2001.

questions.subject: Literature
questions.question: In Greek mythology, the god of the sea is:
questions.explanation: Poseidon rules the sea, Zeus the sky, and Hades the underworld. His Roman counterpart is Neptune.

questions.subject: Literature
questions.question: Thor, the god of thunder, belongs to which mythology?
questions.explanation: Thor is a Norse god, son of Odin, who wields the hammer Mjölnir.

questions.subject: Literature
questions.question: Which Filipino poet, who wrote under the pen name "Doveglion", is known for his "comma poems"?
questions.explanation: Jose Garcia Villa, a National Artist for Literature, placed a comma after almost every word in some poems to regulate their pace.

questions.subject: Literature
questions.question: "America Is in the Heart", about the hard lives of Filipino migrant workers in the United States, was written by:
questions.explanation: Carlos Bulosan's semi-autobiographical book (1946) draws on his own experience as a migrant worker in America.

questions.subject: Literature
questions.question: "Things Fall Apart", a novel about an Igbo community and the effects of colonialism, was written by:
questions.explanation: Chinua Achebe of Nigeria published Things Fall Apart in 1958; it follows Okonkwo as missionaries and colonial rule change his village.

questions.subject: Literature
questions.question: Rabindranath Tagore, the first Asian to win the Nobel Prize in Literature (1913), is best known for the poetry collection:
questions.explanation: Gitanjali ("Song Offerings") won Tagore the Nobel Prize. The Rubaiyat is by Omar Khayyam, and the Ramayana is attributed to Valmiki.

questions.subject: Literature
questions.question: "The Tale of Genji", often called one of the world's first novels, was written by:
questions.explanation: Murasaki Shikibu, a lady of the Heian court in Japan, wrote the Tale of Genji in the early 11th century. Sei Shōnagon wrote The Pillow Book.

questions.subject: Literature
questions.question: "Paradise Lost", an epic poem about the fall of Adam and Eve, was written by:
questions.explanation: John Milton published Paradise Lost in 1667. Chaucer wrote The Canterbury Tales.

questions.subject: Literature
questions.question: Who wrote the poem "The Road Not Taken"?
questions.explanation: Robert Frost published "The Road Not Taken" in 1916; it reflects on choices and their consequences.

questions.subject: Literature
questions.question: A short story with animal characters that teaches a moral lesson, such as "The Tortoise and the Hare", is a:
questions.explanation: Fables, such as Aesop's, use animals that act like people and end with a moral. Legends explain the origin of things or tell of heroes; myths involve gods.

questions.subject: Literature
questions.question: A novel that follows a young character's growth from youth to maturity is called a:
questions.explanation: A bildungsroman, or coming-of-age novel, traces the moral and psychological growth of its main character. An epistolary novel is told through letters.

questions.subject: Literature
questions.question: Very short stories of a few hundred words or less, popular online, are called:
questions.explanation: Flash fiction tells a complete story in very few words. A novella is longer than a short story but shorter than a novel.

questions.subject: Teaching English
questions.question: Learners respond with body movements to commands such as "Stand up" and "Touch your nose". This method is:
questions.explanation: Total Physical Response (James Asher) links language to physical action, which works well for beginners and young learners.

questions.subject: Teaching English
questions.question: Repetition drills, pattern practice and memorized dialogues, based on behaviorism, are features of the:
questions.explanation: The Audio-Lingual Method treats language learning as habit formation through repetition and reinforcement.

questions.subject: Teaching English
questions.question: Learners plan a class trip in English by comparing prices and agreeing on a schedule; the teacher focuses on language forms after the task. This is:
questions.explanation: In Task-Based Language Teaching, a meaningful task with a real outcome comes first, and attention to form follows.

questions.subject: Teaching English
questions.question: Asking learners what they already know about a topic before they read mainly activates their:
questions.explanation: Schema theory holds that readers understand new text by connecting it to what they already know, so pre-reading questions improve comprehension.

questions.subject: Teaching English
questions.question: Asking "Why do you think the character lied?" when the story does not say why targets which level of comprehension?
questions.explanation: Inferential comprehension means reading between the lines to reach ideas the text implies. Literal comprehension is recalling what the text states.

questions.subject: Teaching English
questions.question: In process writing, reorganizing ideas and improving the content of a first draft is called:
questions.explanation: Revising changes content and organization. Editing, which comes after, fixes grammar, spelling and mechanics.

questions.subject: Teaching English
questions.question: Learners listen to an announcement only to find out what time a bus leaves. This practices:
wrong: Listening for gist or main idea
questions.explanation: Listening for specific information means attending only to the particular details needed, such as a departure time, and ignoring the rest. Listening for gist means getting the general idea.

questions.subject: Teaching English
questions.question: An activity in which learners speak smoothly and naturally, without stopping to correct every error, mainly develops:
questions.explanation: Fluency activities focus on getting meaning across easily. Accuracy activities focus on correct forms.

questions.subject: Teaching English
questions.question: An approach in which learners share their personal reactions to and interpretations of a poem is:
questions.explanation: Reader-response theory holds that meaning is created in the interaction between the reader and the text.

questions.subject: Teaching English
questions.question: Analyzing a poem only through its imagery, structure and language, without looking at the author's life, is:
questions.explanation: Formalism (New Criticism) focuses on the text itself: its form, devices and structure.

questions.subject: Teaching English
questions.question: Examining how a novel portrays women and gender roles uses:
questions.explanation: Feminist criticism looks at how literature represents women and gender, and at the power relations behind those representations.

questions.subject: Teaching English
questions.question: Reading a story as an example of the hero's journey, a pattern found in myths around the world, uses:
questions.explanation: Archetypal criticism looks for recurring patterns, characters and symbols, such as the hero's quest, that appear across cultures.

questions.subject: Teaching English
questions.question: Analyzing how an author's word choice, sentence length and figures of speech create a story's tone is called:
questions.explanation: Stylistics studies how linguistic choices in a text create meaning and effect.

questions.subject: Teaching English
questions.question: Studying how speakers take turns, open and close conversations, and repair misunderstandings is part of:
questions.explanation: Discourse analysis, including conversation analysis, studies language in use beyond the single sentence.

questions.subject: Teaching English
questions.question: Which law promotes the development of campus journalism in Philippine schools?
questions.explanation: RA 7079, the Campus Journalism Act of 1991, supports student publications and press freedom in schools.

questions.subject: Teaching English
questions.question: A straight news story puts the most important information first and less important details later. This structure is called the:
questions.explanation: The inverted pyramid lets readers get the key facts quickly and lets editors cut from the bottom.

questions.subject: Teaching English
questions.question: The opening paragraph of a news story, which gives the most important facts and usually answers who, what, when, where, why and how, is the:
questions.explanation: The lead summarizes the most important facts. The byline names the writer, and the dateline gives where (and sometimes when) the story was filed.

questions.subject: Teaching English
questions.question: Which qualities matter most in technical writing?
questions.explanation: Technical writing helps readers understand or do something, so it must be clear, precise and to the point.

questions.subject: Teaching English
questions.question: Teaching nurses the English they need for patient care and medical records is an example of:
questions.explanation: English for Specific Purposes designs lessons around the language needs of a particular field or job.

questions.subject: Teaching English
questions.question: DepEd teachers use the Philippine Informal Reading Inventory (Phil-IRI) to:
questions.correct: Find learners' reading levels and who needs reading intervention
wrong: Grade the final examinations in English and Filipino
Select the honor students for each grade level
Evaluate teachers' performance in teaching reading
questions.explanation: The Phil-IRI assesses word reading and comprehension to place learners at frustration, instructional or independent level and plan help.

questions.subject: Teaching English
questions.question: Translating a text word for word, keeping the original structure even when it sounds unnatural, is:
questions.explanation: Literal translation follows the source closely. Free translation keeps the meaning but uses natural expressions of the target language.

questions.subject: Teaching English
questions.question: In creative writing, "show, don't tell" means:
questions.correct: Use actions and details instead of stating feelings directly
wrong: Use only dialogue, so the characters tell the whole story
Avoid description, so readers can imagine the scene freely
State the story's moral clearly at the very beginning
questions.explanation: Instead of "She was nervous", a writer shows it: "She twisted her ring and kept checking the door."

questions.subject: Teaching English
questions.question: Using a local news article about a recent flood in the community for a reading lesson is an example of:
questions.explanation: Contextualized and localized materials connect lessons to learners' own surroundings, which makes them more meaningful.

questions.subject: Teaching English
questions.question: Reading a literary piece aloud with expression to bring out its meaning, usually with the text in hand, is called:
questions.explanation: Oral interpretation communicates a literary text to listeners through voice and gesture; the reader interprets, not memorizes, the work.

questions.subject: Teaching English
questions.question: A speech given with little or no time to prepare is called:
questions.explanation: An impromptu speech is delivered on the spot. An extemporaneous speech is prepared and outlined but not read word for word.

questions.subject: Mathematical Concepts and History
questions.question: The theorem a² + b² = c² for right triangles is named after:
questions.explanation: The Pythagorean theorem is named after the Greek mathematician Pythagoras, though the relationship was known earlier in Babylon and India.

questions.subject: Mathematical Concepts and History
questions.question: The word "algebra" comes from the title of a book by:
questions.explanation: Al-Khwarizmi's 9th-century book on "al-jabr" (restoring) gave algebra its name. The word "algorithm" also comes from his name.

questions.subject: Mathematical Concepts and History
questions.question: The sequence 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, ..., in which each term is the sum of the two before it, is named after:
