questions.subject: Teaching Mathematics
questions.question: After learning the area of a rectangle, learners find the area of an L-shaped room by dividing it into rectangles. In a 5E lesson, this is the:
questions.explanation: In Elaborate, learners apply what they learned to a new, more complex situation. Explain is where the concept and terms are formally developed.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: "Learners who eat breakfast score higher on tests, so giving every learner a free school breakfast will raise test scores." Which statement, if true, most weakens this argument?
questions.correct: Learners who eat breakfast at home also tend to sleep longer and get more study help at home
wrong: Some learners do not like the food that the school breakfast program would serve
The breakfast program would cost the school about two million pesos every year
Test scores in a nearby school rose last year even without a breakfast program
questions.explanation: The argument assumes breakfast causes higher scores. If breakfast-eaters also differ in sleep and home support, those factors may explain the scores, so the free breakfast might not help. Cost and menu complaints do not touch the causal claim.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which sentence uses "lay" and "lie" correctly?
questions.correct: After she had laid the books on the table, she lay down to rest.
wrong: After she had laid the books on the table, she laid down to rest.
After she had lain the books on the table, she lay down to rest.
After she had lain the books on the table, she laid down to rest.
questions.explanation: "Lay" takes an object (lay, laid, laid): she had laid the books. "Lie" (to recline) takes none (lie, lay, lain): she lay down. The past of "lie" is "lay", which is why the two verbs are so often confused.

questions.subject: Science and Technology
questions.question: A block has a mass of 300 g and a volume of 400 cm³. Water has a density of 1 g/cm³. What happens when the block is placed in water?
questions.correct: It floats, with about 75% of its volume under water
wrong: It floats, with about 25% of its volume under water
It sinks, because its mass is more than its volume in water
It stays suspended halfway, neither floating nor sinking
questions.explanation: Density = 300 ÷ 400 = 0.75 g/cm³, less than water's, so it floats. A floating object sinks until it displaces its own mass of water: 300 cm³, which is 75% of its volume.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: A store marks up an item 40% above its cost, then sells it at a 20% discount from the marked price. What is its profit as a percent of the cost?
questions.explanation: Selling price = cost × 1.40 × 0.80 = 1.12 × cost, so the profit is 12% of the cost. Subtracting the percents (40% − 20%) gives 20%, which ignores that the discount is taken from the higher marked price.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Two cars leave the same place at the same time and drive in opposite directions at 60 km/h and 40 km/h. After how many hours will they be 350 km apart?
questions.explanation: Moving apart, their speeds add: 60 + 40 = 100 km/h, so 350 ÷ 100 = 3.5 hours. 17.5 hours would be the answer if they drove in the same direction (difference of 20 km/h).

questions.subject: Philippine History
questions.question: A diary said to be written by a Katipunero in 1896 mentions an event that happened three years after his recorded death. What should a historian conclude?
questions.correct: The diary, or at least that passage, may not be authentic and must be examined further
wrong: The event must really have happened earlier than historians have recorded
The diary is reliable, since it came from the time of the Revolution
The writer must have correctly predicted the event years in advance
questions.explanation: An anachronism, something the supposed author could not have known, is a warning sign in external criticism. The passage may be a later addition or the whole diary a forgery; it must be checked before use.

questions.subject: Philippine History
questions.question: Filipinos had fought Spain alongside the Americans in 1898. Why did war break out between Filipinos and Americans in 1899?
questions.correct: Spain ceded the islands to the US in the Treaty of Paris, and the US did not recognize the Filipino republic
wrong: The US objected to the Malolos Constitution's use of Tagalog as the official language
Aguinaldo refused to let American ships stop in Manila Bay after the Spanish fleet was defeated
Spain refused to leave Manila, so the Americans blamed the Filipinos for the delay
questions.explanation: Under the Treaty of Paris (December 1898), Spain ceded the Philippines to the United States for 20 million dollars without Filipino participation. The US treated the islands as its territory, the First Republic opposed this, and fighting began on February 4, 1899.

questions.subject: Philippine History
questions.question: Which feature of the 1987 Constitution most directly answers the experience of martial law under Marcos?
questions.correct: Martial law is limited to 60 days, Congress may revoke it, and the Supreme Court may review its basis
wrong: The President may issue decrees with the force of law whenever Congress is not in session
A parliamentary system replaces the presidency, with a prime minister as head of government
A single-chamber Batasang Pambansa holds both legislative and executive powers
questions.explanation: Article VII, Section 18 limits martial law and lets Congress and the Supreme Court check it. Decree-making power, a parliamentary form and the Batasang Pambansa belong to the 1973 Constitution as amended under Marcos.

questions.subject: Life and Works of Rizal
questions.question: At the end of El Filibusterismo, Simoun's plan for a violent uprising fails, and Padre Florentino says that freedom must be won through virtue and sacrifice. What does this ending suggest about Rizal's view?
questions.correct: He doubted a revolution could succeed before the people were morally and educationally ready
wrong: He fully supported an immediate armed uprising led by wealthy Filipinos like Simoun
He expected Spain to grant independence peacefully within a few years
He believed that Filipinos should give up all hope of reform and accept Spanish rule
questions.explanation: The failure of Simoun's selfish, vengeful plan and Florentino's final speech are usually read as Rizal's warning that independence needs a prepared, virtuous people, not as a rejection of all change.

questions.subject: Life and Works of Rizal
questions.question: A historian argues that Rizal was a reformist, not a revolutionary. Which piece of evidence best supports this?
questions.correct: His December 1896 manifesto from prison condemned the uprising and urged education first
wrong: The Katipunan used his name as a password and hung his portrait at its meetings
His second novel describes a wealthy man secretly planning an armed uprising
He was tried by a Spanish court-martial and executed for rebellion and sedition
questions.explanation: Rizal's own statement rejecting the uprising directly supports the reformist view. The Katipunan's use of his name, the plot of the Fili and his conviction could all be used to argue the opposite, or say nothing about his own intent.

questions.subject: Ethics
questions.question: A company pays its workers far below a living wage, treating them only as tools for profit. Which principle does this most directly violate?
questions.correct: Kant's formula of humanity: never treat persons merely as a means
wrong: Kant's formula of universal law: act only on rules everyone could follow
The hypothetical imperative: act to reach the goals you have chosen
Mill's principle of utility: act for the greatest happiness overall
questions.explanation: Using people only as instruments, without respecting them as ends in themselves, is exactly what the formula of humanity forbids. Universal law is another formulation of the categorical imperative, but it tests whether a rule could be willed for everyone.

questions.subject: Ethics
questions.question: "Most people in our town accept vote-buying, so accepting money for your vote is morally right." What is the main flaw in this argument?
questions.correct: It draws a moral conclusion only from what people commonly do or accept
wrong: It attacks the character of the person who opposes vote-buying
It assumes that only two choices are possible when there are more
It claims that one small step will lead to a chain of disasters
questions.explanation: An argument that moves from what is done or accepted to what ought to be done (an appeal to common practice) is invalid: widespread acceptance does not make an act right. The other options describe ad hominem, false dilemma and slippery slope.

questions.subject: The Contemporary World
questions.question: The peso weakens from ₱50 to ₱58 per US dollar. Which outcome is most likely?
questions.correct: OFW families get more pesos for each dollar, but imported goods such as fuel cost more
wrong: Imported goods become cheaper, while OFW families get fewer pesos for each dollar
OFW remittances lose value in pesos, and Philippine exports cost foreign buyers more
Fuel and other imports cost the same, since their prices are set in pesos
questions.explanation: Each dollar now buys more pesos, so remittances are worth more at home. But imports priced in dollars need more pesos, so they cost more, and Philippine exports become cheaper for foreign buyers.

questions.subject: Art Appreciation
questions.question: A critic says, "This painting is excellent because it captures exactly how the subject really looks." This judgment reflects which theory of art?
questions.explanation: Imitationalism values art for realistic representation. Formalism judges the organization of elements and principles; emotionalism, the feelings the work expresses or evokes; instrumentalism, the work's social or moral purpose.

questions.subject: Art Appreciation
questions.question: In a mural, a farmer is painted much larger than the landlord standing right beside him, to show the farmer's importance. This is:
questions.explanation: Hierarchical proportion makes figures larger according to their importance, not their real size or distance. Linear perspective would make the nearer figure larger, but here the two stand side by side.

questions.subject: Understanding the Self
questions.question: A student with good grades compares herself only with the class valedictorian and feels she is failing. In Festinger's theory, this is:
questions.explanation: Comparing oneself with someone who seems better is upward comparison; it can motivate but also lower self-esteem. Downward comparison is with someone worse off; the looking-glass self is about imagined judgments of others.

questions.subject: The Teaching Profession
questions.question: A publisher offers a teacher free seminars if she requires her learners to buy its review books. What should she do?
questions.correct: Decline, because a benefit for requiring materials is a conflict of interest
wrong: Accept, as long as the review books are of good quality and fairly priced
Accept, as long as the school head approves the arrangement in writing
Accept, but tell parents that buying the books is optional this year
questions.explanation: The Code of Ethics bars teachers from accepting favors in exchange for concessions and from using their position for personal gain. Quality, approval or calling the books optional does not remove the conflict of interest created by the offer.

questions.subject: The Teaching Profession
questions.question: A school places most learners from poor families in the lowest sections, which get the least experienced teachers. Which perspective would most likely criticize this as serving the interests of advantaged groups?
questions.explanation: Conflict theory examines how school structures maintain inequality between groups. Functionalism would tend to see sorting as efficient matching of learners to roles; symbolic interactionism would focus on labels in everyday interaction.

questions.subject: Curriculum and Teaching Methods
questions.question: An objective says learners will "evaluate the credibility of online news sources," but the unit test asks them only to list the types of news sources. What is the main problem?
questions.correct: The test measures recall, a lower level than the evaluating the objective requires
wrong: The test is too difficult, since evaluating sources is beyond most learners
The objective is not measurable, since credibility cannot be assessed
The test is unreliable, since listing items is hard to score consistently
questions.explanation: Constructive alignment requires the assessment to match the objective's level. Listing is remembering, while the objective is at the evaluating level; learners should judge real sources against criteria.

questions.subject: Curriculum and Teaching Methods
questions.question: In a 4A's lesson, learners first measure shadows outdoors, then discuss what they noticed. At which step should the teacher ask, "What general rule can we form from your observations?"
questions.explanation: The 4A's are Activity (the experience), Analysis (processing what happened), Abstraction (forming the concept or generalization) and Application (using it in new situations). Forming the rule is abstraction.

questions.subject: Child and Adolescent Learners
questions.question: Teacher A waits until learners show they are developmentally ready before teaching abstract ideas. Teacher B teaches slightly above learners' current level with support. Their views follow, in order:
questions.explanation: Piaget held that development must come before certain learning, so teaching waits for readiness. Vygotsky held that learning with support in the zone of proximal development leads development forward.

questions.subject: Child and Adolescent Learners
questions.question: A learner's tantrums keep increasing because the teacher lets him skip his work whenever he has one. What is happening, and what should the teacher do?
questions.correct: It negatively reinforces the tantrums; stop the skipping and reward calm requests
wrong: Skipping work punishes the tantrums; allow even longer breaks so they stop sooner
Skipping work positively reinforces the tantrums; add more work after each tantrum
The tantrums show a lack of attention; give him more praise during each tantrum
questions.explanation: Removing an unpleasant task after a tantrum increases tantrums, which is negative reinforcement. The fix is to remove that payoff and reinforce an acceptable way to ask for a break. Praising tantrums would reinforce them further.

questions.subject: Child and Adolescent Learners
questions.question: A learner argues that the school dress code should be changed through the student council, because rules are agreements meant to serve the students and can be revised when they no longer do. Which Kohlberg stage does this reasoning show?
questions.explanation: Seeing rules as agreements that serve people and can be changed by fair process is stage 5. Stage 4 would uphold the rule because rules keep order, whatever one thinks of them.

questions.subject: Child and Adolescent Learners
questions.question: A 17-year-old is trying out different clubs, part-time jobs and possible college courses but has not yet decided on any. In Marcia's terms, she is in:
questions.explanation: Moratorium is active exploration without commitment yet. Diffusion would mean neither exploring nor committing; foreclosure, committing without exploring; achievement, committing after exploring.

questions.subject: Assessment of Learning
questions.question: An item has a difficulty index of 0.92 and a discrimination index of 0.05. What should the teacher do?
questions.correct: Revise or replace it, since almost everyone got it right and it barely separates high and low scorers
wrong: Keep it, since a high difficulty index shows that the item is valid and well written
Keep it, since any discrimination index above zero means the item works well
Make it harder by adding a fifth option, since the index is already acceptable
questions.explanation: p = 0.92 means the item is very easy, and D = 0.05 means high and low scorers did almost equally well. An item that tells the teacher almost nothing about who has mastered the content should be revised or replaced.

questions.subject: Language and Linguistics
questions.question: A manager says "It's cold in here," and an assistant closes the window. In Austin's terms, the request to close the window is the utterance's:
questions.explanation: The locutionary act is saying the words with their literal meaning; the illocutionary act is what the speaker does by saying them (here, requesting); the perlocutionary act is the effect on the listener (the window is closed).

questions.subject: Teaching English
questions.question: Which sequence follows Willis's framework for task-based language teaching?
questions.correct: Pre-task, then the task cycle of task, planning and report, then language focus
wrong: Language focus, then pre-task, then the task cycle of task, planning and report
Presentation of the form, then controlled practice, then a free speaking task
Task cycle of task, planning and report, then pre-task, then language focus
questions.explanation: In Willis's framework, learners first meet the topic (pre-task), do and report on a task, and only then study the language forms that came up. The third option describes PPP, which puts form first.

questions.subject: Teaching English
questions.question: Two English teachers score the same essays and give very different grades. What would best improve the scores' reliability?
questions.correct: Use one analytic rubric and calibrate on sample essays before scoring
wrong: Let each teacher use her own rubric, then average the two grades
Shorten the essays so that scoring takes less time
Replace the essay with a multiple-choice grammar test
questions.explanation: Inter-rater reliability improves when raters share criteria and agree on what each level looks like, using anchor papers. Changing to multiple choice raises reliability but no longer measures writing, which harms validity.

questions.subject: Teaching English
questions.question: Which activity fits a formalist approach to Frost's "The Road Not Taken"?
questions.correct: Trace how the images of the roads and the rhyme scheme build meaning
wrong: Write about a difficult choice in your own life and how it felt
Research Frost's friendship with the poet who inspired the poem
Discuss how the poem reflects American ideas of individualism
questions.explanation: Formalism studies the text itself: imagery, structure, sound and form. The other activities are reader-response (personal experience), biographical (the author's life) and cultural or historical criticism.

questions.subject: Teaching English
questions.question: All the passages in a reading test are about basketball, and learners who play basketball score higher. What is the main problem?
questions.correct: Topic bias, which weakens validity and fairness
wrong: Low reliability caused by too few test items
Poor practicality caused by long passages
A lack of washback on classroom teaching
questions.explanation: The test partly measures background knowledge of basketball, not only reading ability. That threatens validity and fairness; it says nothing about reliability, practicality or washback.

questions.subject: Mathematical Concepts and History
questions.question: What is the negation of "If a figure is a square, then it is a rectangle"?
questions.correct: A figure is a square and it is not a rectangle.
wrong: If a figure is not a square, then it is not a rectangle.
If a figure is a rectangle, then it is a square.
If a figure is not a rectangle, then it is not a square.
questions.explanation: A conditional "if p, then q" is false only when p is true and q is false, so its negation is "p and not q". The other options are the inverse, the converse and the contrapositive, which are conditionals themselves.

questions.subject: Problem Solving
questions.question: A rectangle's length is 3 cm more than its width, and its area is 70 cm². What is its perimeter?
questions.explanation: w(w + 3) = 70 gives w² + 3w − 70 = 0, so (w + 10)(w − 7) = 0 and w = 7 (width cannot be negative). Length = 10, perimeter = 2(7 + 10) = 34 cm. 17 cm is half the perimeter.

questions.subject: Problem Solving
questions.question: A substance has a half-life of 5 days. How much of an 80 g sample remains after 20 days?
questions.explanation: 20 days is 4 half-lives: 80 → 40 → 20 → 10 → 5 g. Dividing 80 by 4 gives 20 g, which treats the decay as linear.

questions.subject: Problem Solving
questions.question: Solve |2x − 3| < 5.
questions.explanation: |2x − 3| < 5 means −5 < 2x − 3 < 5, so −2 < 2x < 8 and −1 < x < 4. "Or" answers belong to "greater than" absolute value inequalities.

questions.subject: Problem Solving
questions.question: y varies directly as x and inversely as the square of z. If y = 6 when x = 4 and z = 2, what is y when x = 6 and z = 3?
questions.explanation: y = kx/z²: 6 = k(4)/4, so k = 6. Then y = 6(6)/9 = 4. Forgetting to square z gives 6; ignoring z gives 9.

questions.subject: Problem Solving
questions.question: A fair coin is tossed 4 times. What is the probability of getting exactly 2 heads?
questions.explanation: There are 2⁴ = 16 equally likely outcomes, and C(4, 2) = 6 have exactly two heads: 6/16 = 3/8. "Half the tosses are heads" makes 1/2 tempting, but exactly two is less likely than that.

questions.subject: Problem Solving
questions.question: What is the area of the triangle with vertices (0, 0), (6, 0) and (2, 5)?
questions.explanation: The base from (0, 0) to (6, 0) is 6, and the height is the y-coordinate of (2, 5), which is 5. Area = ½ × 6 × 5 = 15. Forgetting the ½ gives 30.

questions.subject: Curriculum and Teaching Methods
questions.question: Which DepEd issuance sets the policy guidelines for implementing the MATATAG Curriculum?
questions.explanation: DO No. 010, s. 2024, issued on July 23, 2024, contains the Policy Guidelines on the Implementation of the MATATAG Curriculum. DO 8, s. 2015 is on classroom assessment, DO 42, s. 2017 is the PPST, and DO 40, s. 2012 is the Child Protection Policy.

questions.subject: Curriculum and Teaching Methods
questions.question: In which grade levels did the MATATAG Curriculum begin in School Year 2024–2025?
wrong: All grades from Kindergarten to Grade 10
questions.explanation: DO No. 010, s. 2024 phases the curriculum in, starting in SY 2024–2025 with Kindergarten and Grades 1, 4 and 7, followed by the other grade levels in the next school years.

questions.subject: Curriculum and Teaching Methods
questions.question: Under DO No. 010, s. 2024, what happens to the Senior High School curriculum for now?
questions.correct: It stays in effect until a separate order on Grades 11 and 12 is issued
wrong: It shifted to the MATATAG Curriculum together with Grade 7
It was replaced by college-preparatory courses
Grades 11 and 12 were removed from basic education
questions.explanation: DO 010 covers only Kindergarten to Grade 10. DepEd's FAQ states that a separate order will cover Grades 11 and 12, and that the current SHS curriculum (DO 21, s. 2019) and SHS MELCs remain in effect meanwhile.

questions.subject: Curriculum and Teaching Methods
questions.question: How does Grade 1 under the MATATAG Curriculum differ from Grade 1 under the 2016 K to 12 curriculum?
questions.correct: It has five learning areas instead of seven, focused on literacy and numeracy
wrong: It has seven learning areas, the same as before, but with fewer hours
It has five learning areas, focused on science and technology
It has nine learning areas, adding Mother Tongue and Makabansa
questions.explanation: DepEd's General Shaping Paper explains that Grade 1 shifted from seven learning areas to five to strengthen literacy and numeracy: Language, Reading and Literacy, Mathematics, Makabansa, and GMRC.

questions.subject: Curriculum and Teaching Methods
questions.question: Which best describes Makabansa in the MATATAG Curriculum?
questions.correct: A transdisciplinary Grades 1–3 area on civics, history, culture and health
wrong: A Grade 7 elective on Philippine politics, government and citizenship
A reading program for Grade 1 learners at the frustration level
A values subject that replaced GMRC in all grade levels from K to 10
questions.explanation: Makabansa is a new learning area for Key Stage 1 (Grades 1 to 3). It uses a transdisciplinary approach to civics, history, art and culture, and health and wellness, and prepares learners for Music and Arts, PE and Health, and Araling Panlipunan in later grades.

questions.subject: Curriculum and Teaching Methods
questions.question: Under the MATATAG Curriculum, what happened to Mother Tongue as a learning area?
questions.correct: It is no longer taught as a separate learning area
wrong: It became a required learning area from Grades 1 to 6
It replaced Filipino as a learning area in Grades 1 to 3
It moved to Senior High School as an elective
questions.explanation: DepEd's FAQ on DO 010, s. 2024 states that Mother Tongue is no longer a learning area. (Which language is used to teach in the early grades is a separate question; RA 12027 of 2024 later changed that rule.)

questions.subject: Curriculum and Teaching Methods
questions.question: A school head says that schools using the MATATAG Curriculum must switch to a new grading system right away. Is this correct?
questions.correct: No; DO 8, s. 2015 stays in effect until a new assessment policy is issued
wrong: Yes; DO 010, s. 2024 replaced DO 8, s. 2015 for all grade levels
Yes; MATATAG schools now use pass-or-fail marks instead of grades
No; MATATAG schools no longer give grades in Grades 1 to 3
questions.explanation: DepEd's FAQ states that DO 8, s. 2015 remains in effect until a new policy on assessment is released, as provided in DO 010, s. 2024.

questions.subject: Curriculum and Teaching Methods
questions.question: DepEd's curriculum review found that typically fewer than 20% of teachers had enough time to teach all the learning competencies set for a quarter. Which MATATAG feature responds most directly to this finding?
questions.correct: Decongesting the curriculum by reducing the number of learning competencies
wrong: Embedding peace competencies across the learning areas
Introducing Makabansa as a new learning area in Grades 1 to 3
Starting the rollout with Kindergarten and Grades 1, 4 and 7
questions.explanation: All four are real MATATAG features, but only decongesting the curriculum answers a lack of time to teach every competency. DepEd's review recommended reducing the number of competencies so each can be taught with the required depth in the time available.

questions.subject: Curriculum and Teaching Methods
questions.question: Which is NOT one of the four components of DepEd's MATATAG agenda?
questions.correct: Make Senior High School optional for all learners
wrong: Make the curriculum relevant to produce competent, job-ready citizens
Take good care of learners by promoting their well-being
Give support to teachers to teach better
questions.explanation: The MATATAG agenda ("Bansang Makabata, Batang Makabansa") has four components: MAke the curriculum relevant; TAke steps to accelerate delivery of basic education facilities and services; TAke good care of learners; and Give support to teachers to teach better.
